summary: Luke Merrett describes why he uses Workflowy for brainstorming but needs scheduling, repeating tasks and reminders that it lacks, so he built a Selenium script in Python that logs in, finds items tagged with today's date, and adds a #Focus tag so he can search for daily work. The script runs automatically when he logs in to his machine. He also outlines two planned extensions: duplicating repeating items and sending email or Slack notifications for reminders, and invites contributions on GitHub.
one_line: Luke Merrett's Selenium-based Python script that automatically tags Workflowy items with today's date as #Focus, adding scheduling to the outlining tool.
key_facts: Workflowy is described as an outlining tool that allows users to create large hierarchies of bullet points.
Workflowy lacks scheduled items, repeating tasks, and reminders, which the author considers essential for task management.
Workflowy does not expose any API, so the author turned to Selenium to automate the process.
The script launches Firefox, logs in to Workflowy, finds items with a tag matching today's date (e.g. #2016-02-18), and gives each a #Focus tag.
The author schedules the script to run as a scheduled task when he logs in to his machine.
The author previously used NirvanaHQ and Todoist as primary task apps alongside Workflowy for brainstorming.
The script's wait helper uses WebDriverWait with a 10-second timeout until a CSS selector element appears.
The script sends the END key before appending the tag so the cursor moves to the end of the existing text.
The first planned extension is to find and duplicate repeating items tagged #Repeating, such as #DailyAt17:00.
The second planned extension is to notify the user by email or Slack when an item reminder is triggered.
The author notes that Workflowy bullet points have static links, so an email could link directly to the item.
The article was published on February 18, 2016 and takes about 3 minutes to read.
The script code is hosted on GitHub at lukemerrett/Workflowy-Automation.
